compute_stock.title: Installed AI compute
compute_stock.blurb: Total AI compute ever shipped, summed across all chip designers.

scenarios.name: Floor — 1.5×/yr
scenarios.note: Compute growth decelerates hard to 1.5×/yr (a conservative floor).

scenarios.name: Central — 3.3×→1.5×/yr
scenarios.note: Recent ~3.3×/yr decaying linearly to 1.5×/yr by 2031 (Epoch/brief style).

scenarios.name: No slowdown — 3.3×/yr
scenarios.note: Today's ~3.3×/yr pace simply continues — almost certainly hits power/packaging limits first.

fleet_power.title: AI fleet power draw
fleet_power.blurb: Total power of all AI silicon. 'Facility' adds the ~2.5x overhead (servers, networking, cooling).

projection.note: Power = installed compute ÷ chip energy-efficiency gains (~1.34×/yr). Each power scenario tracks the matching install scenario.

compute_by_source.title: Cumulative AI compute by chip designer
compute_by_source.blurb: Where the installed compute comes from — cumulative H100-equivalents by chip designer. NVIDIA dominates; custom silicon (Google, Amazon) and AMD are the challengers.

nvidia_production.title: NVIDIA AI-chip production by generation
nvidia_production.blurb: Estimated units shipped by GPU generation. Unit count plateaued ~1.2M/q — growth is compute per chip, not chip count. NVIDIA publishes no unit data; Epoch estimate.

nvidia_total.title: NVIDIA total chip production
nvidia_total.blurb: Total units shipped per quarter (sum across generations) — the smooth total behind the generational split.
nvidia_total.source: Epoch AI — AI Chip Sales (CC-BY); forecast = stated growth assumptions

scenarios.name: Flat (~CoWoS-limited)
scenarios.note: Unit count stays ~flat — bigger chips eat the extra packaging.

scenarios.name: +15%/yr
scenarios.note: Modest unit growth on top of mix shift to bigger chips.

scenarios.name: +30%/yr
scenarios.note: Aggressive: units and per-chip capability both climb fast.

component_share.title: AI's share of the chip supply chain
component_share.blurb: AI accelerators already consume nearly all of the world's advanced packaging (CoWoS) and HBM memory.

compute_trends.title: Compute per chip, by numeric precision
compute_trends.blurb: Per-chip performance (log) by precision. Filled points are the frontier; stars are announced roadmap parts.

chip_power.title: Power per chip (TDP)
chip_power.blurb: Thermal design power per accelerator. Each generation does more compute — and draws more power.

chip_efficiency.title: Energy efficiency (FP16 per watt)
chip_efficiency.blurb: Tensor-FP16 throughput per watt — the deflator on power. Improving, but slower than per-chip compute climbs.

tsmc_monthly.title: TSMC monthly revenue
tsmc_monthly.blurb: The foundry's monthly revenue (reported ~the 10th) — the highest-frequency public read on AI-chip demand. Converted to US$ (~31 NT$/US$).

odm_revenue.title: AI-server makers' monthly revenue (Taiwan)
odm_revenue.blurb: ODMs (original design manufacturers) build the AI servers and racks for the cloud giants. Each NVIDIA generation shows up as a step-up in their revenue; the Rubin wave is the next to watch.

nvidia_commitments.title: NVIDIA forward supply commitments
nvidia_commitments.blurb: Cash NVIDIA has pre-committed to suppliers (HBM/CoWoS/wafers) — the earliest leading indicator, leading chips by quarters.

micron_cmbu.title: Micron Cloud Memory: revenue & margin (HBM-driven)
micron_cmbu.blurb: The best primary numeric HBM proxy from filings — Micron's HBM/data-centre segment (Micron ~20% of the HBM market). Operating margin shows the pricing-power surge.
micron_cmbu.source: Micron 10-Q (CMBU segment), parsed from SEC EDGAR

tsmc_hpc.title: TSMC HPC-platform revenue
tsmc_hpc.blurb: TSMC's HPC (AI/datacentre) platform as a share of the world's leading foundry. The light line is a log-linear fit on 2022+ history, drawn back through the points and extrapolated to 2030.
tsmc_hpc.source: TSMC 20-F (platform revenue), parsed from SEC EDGAR; NT$ at ~31/US$

euv_units.title: EUV machines made per year
euv_units.blurb: Every leading-edge AI chip needs EUV lithography — made by one company (ASML). Units (NXE+EXE) parsed from ASML 20-Fs.
euv_units.source: ASML 20-F (net system sales per technology), parsed from SEC EDGAR

skhynix.title: SK Hynix — the HBM leader
skhynix.blurb: World #1 HBM maker (~62% share, ~70% of Rubin HBM4). Revenue converted to US$ (~1,350 ₩/US$).
skhynix.source: SK Hynix quarterly financials via Yahoo Finance (000660.KS)

korea_memory.title: Korea memory-chip exports
korea_memory.blurb: Korea (SK Hynix + Samsung ≈ 70% of global DRAM/HBM) memory-IC exports — a customs-verified, near-real-time proxy for the memory & HBM boom.

us_energy.title: US electricity: generation, demand & AI
us_energy.blurb: US electricity generation & demand (monthly) against AI datacentres' annualised draw. A sliver today — but on the central scaling path it chases the whole US grid within years.
us_energy.source: EIA — electric-power-operational-data (generation) + retail-sales (demand), monthly; AI = Epoch fleet power × hours

buildout.title: The buildout — what the compute trend requires
buildout.blurb: Drive AI compute forward and see the physical requirements it implies — wafers, packaging, EUV machines, power, dollars — vs what's actually available. Twizzle the knobs.
buildout.source: Epoch AI (Chip Sales, Components, Frontier Data Centers; CC-BY) + ASML (EUV)
